thread:
incident-bot: 🔔 INCIDENT ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected on inference-gateway (northamerica). Alert rule: 5xx_rate > 10% for 2m. Spikes started ~03:42 UTC. Pager sent to #oncall-sre. Link: https://ops.redwood.example/alerts/INC-1769993333

leo: ack — I'm on it. Paging details?

incident-bot: Root cause hints: spike correlated with a config push to gateway-config (commit f3a9c2b) at 03:40 UTC. Error sample: 502, 503, upstream reset. Affected route: /v1/infer -> target-pool inference-pool-1.

rachel: yep that commit bumped route weight to 60% for inference-pool-1 and increased route retries from 2 -> 5 (we were testing aggressive retries for client timeouts). I rolled the change to canary earlier but it looks like it hit prod during the push.

aj: retries=5 + high fanout -> retry amplification. If upstream is overloaded retries will cascade into 5xx. We should disable retries at the gateway ASAP and set circuit-breaker to failfast.

leo: +1. Oncall plan: 1) set retries to 0 on the gateway route 2) reduce route weight back to previous baseline 3) monitor error rate and latency 4) if not fixed, rollback the config commit.

sam: I'll patch the config. Pushing a quick hotfix to disable retries now.

sre-bot: Executing config patch: PATCH /configs/gateway/routes/infer - payload {"retry_policy": {"num_retries": 0}} (dry-run ok)

sre-bot: Patch applied to prod gateway via cfg-agent (apply id: cfg-rollback-1769993333). Confirming…

maya: sending verification checks — curl to /v1/health on gateway and a few upstreams, tailing envoy logs for 502/503s.

maya: envoy logs (tail):
```
[03:42:31] envoy: upstream reset stream conn_failure host=10.1.4.12: upstream_5xx
[03:42:33] envoy: 502 Bad Gateway from upstream target-pool inference-pool-1
[03:42:34] envoy: request retries: 3 -> amplified
```

leo: good snapshot. Sam, what's the weight now?

sam: rolled weight back to 20% from 60% for inference-pool-1. Command used: `git -C infra/gateway-config revert f3a9c2b && cfg-agent apply --commit HEAD`

aj: also recommend setting circuit breaker max_connections and pending_requests lower so that overloaded hosts refuse fast. Example snippet to apply after immediate triage:
```
circuit_breakers:
  thresholds:
    - priority: DEFAULT
      max_connections: 1000
      max_pending_requests: 50
      max_retries: 0
```

leo: monitoring dashboard: error_rate (5xx) was 18% at peak. After disabling retries and weight rollback: down to 4% within ~90s. Latency p50 stable.

incident-bot: Customer impact estimate: approx 12% of requests in NA hit errors; we have early CS reports for 3 paying customers showing elevated client errors and a few retry storms. No data loss.

rachel: starting an incident severity timeline: start 03:42, mitigation (retries=0 + weight rollback) 03:44, error rate drop observed 03:46.

sam: running a controlled canary for the reverted config to ensure no regressions across regions. Will keep prod unchanged until postmortem.

maya: follow-up checks: tailing logs show residual 5xx from a small subset of hosts (inference-pool-1 node-7) — suspect node-level overload. I recommend cordon/drain that node from pool.

aj: agree. I'll trigger a drain: `poolctl drain inference-pool-1 node-7 --reason "hotfix drain post-retry-amplify"`

ops-bot: Drain initiated for node-7 in inference-pool-1. ETA ~45s to re-route traffic.

leo: good. After drain completes, re-run load test and check p95 latency and 5xx.

maya: drain finished. node-7 removed. 5xx down to ~1.8% now. Looks stable for past 3m.

rachel: immediate customer-facing note: CS team drafted a brief acknowledging transient errors 03:42-03:46 UTC, impact limited to request failures (no data loss), mitigation applied. Will push once incident owner signs off.

leo: owners and next steps: - Incident owner: leo (eng-sre) - Remediation owner (config): sam - Runtime owner (pool health): maya - Postmortem: rachel (prod infra) - Product/customer comms: aj

aj: action items (short term): 1) revert retry policy change in repository and add a stricter rollout gating for retry-related flags, 2) add a canary-only knob for retries, 3) add automated detection to flag retry-amplification patterns (retry_count rise + upstream latency)

rachel: created ticket INF-4823 "Gateway retry policy caused amplification -> rollback + rollout gating" and assigned to eng-runtime and eng-sre. Link: https://tracker.redwood.example/INF-4823

leo: closing the oncall paging — error rates low and healthy baseline restored. We'll keep monitoring for 2 hours. If anything spikes ping @oncall-sre.

incident-bot: Incident resolved (status: mitigated). Summary: incorrect retry policy + route weight pushed in commit f3a9c2b caused retry amplification and overload on inference pool, producing elevated 5xx. Mitigations: disabled retries at gateway, rolled route weight to previous baseline, drained overloaded node. Postmortem ticket INF-4823 filed.

sam: quick note — will follow up with a small automation to block retry increases without product approval.

maya: thanks team.

leo: thanks. tagging this thread for postmortem and follow-up: @eng-runtime @eng-sre @product

sre-bot: Incident log archived: INC-1769993333. Recommended follow-ups: test harness for retry-laden traffic and a KB entry on retry amplification.

aj: assigning myself to the KB and small patch for rollout gating.

rachel: will write the timeline for the postmortem today.

leo: ending thread. Good work all. :thumbsup:
